entries.title: Philippians 3:1
segments: The same things. These were repetitions of his former counsels, to be kept continually in mind on the score of safety.

entries.title: Philippians 3:2
segments: The dogs. This term applies to those of unholy tastes and desires, of whom Jesus warned the multitude in the Sermon on the Mount:-'Give not that which is holy unto the dogs' (

).
 

 
 The concision. The word signifies the mutilation practised by fanatics.  See
.  It is here used by Paul in scorn for the circumcision of the flesh, as being of no greater spiritual importance.

entries.title: Philippians 3:3
segments: For we are the circumcision. The rite of circumcision signified consecration unto God, but it was merely a symbol.  The real consecration was from within.  As Paul says, in
, 'Circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit not in the letter.'  See

entries.title: Philippians 3:7
segments: What things were gain to me. In the two proceding verses Paul enumerates his superior outward qualifications as an orthodox Jew.  These things, while gain from a worldly viewpoint, he counts as 'but refuse' (
) compared with the knowledge of Christ, and 'the righteousness which is from God, by faith' (

entries.title: Philippians 3:10
segments: Conformed unto his death. Paul is not referring to the death on the cross, but that death unto the flesh which resulted in the resurrection.  See

entries.title: Philippians 3:11
segments: If by any means I may attain unto the resurrection from the dead.   This was the goal of Paul's hope, as it was the consummation of the human life of his lord.  See

entries.title: Philippians 3:12
segments: Not that I have already obtained. Paul was working out his own salvation with fear and trembling (see note
), and he permitted no self-confidence to deceive him.

entries.title: Philippians 3:13
segments: Forgetting the things which are behind. Paul had held a position of high honor and influence among the Pharisees at Jerusalem because of his learning, both in literature and the law.  In giving allegiance to Christ he became a despised outcast to his former associates.  See

entries.title: Philippians 3:17
segments: Imitators together of me. The context (
) shows that the imitation urged was as to Paul's attitude toward the things of the world as well as the anxious spirit in which he pressed onward.

entries.title: Philippians 3:18
segments: Enemies of the cross of Christ. These were not of the unbelievers, that some among the brethren.  As the cross is the symbol of self-sacrifice, those who 'mind earthly things' (
) are at enmity to all that the cross stands for.

entries.title: Philippians 3:20
segments: Our citizenship is in heaven. This illustration was drawn from the fact that the citizenship of the Philippian was in Rome.  Paul voiced the same idea in
:- 'for we have not here an abiding city, but we seek after the city which is to come.'

entries.title: Philippians 3:21
segments: The body of our humiliation. This is the body of the flesh which so humiliated Paul, when he declared 'For the good which I would do not: but the evil which I would not, that I practise' (

).
